# Ammo Reference Library: cartridge profiles (ammochart.net)

Typical factory-load figures from https://ammochart.net/. Values vary by brand, lot and barrel length; check the maker's data for your exact load.

## 10mm Auto
URL: https://ammochart.net/cartridges/10mm-auto
Powerful semi-auto round for hog and deer hunting and woods carry against black bear.
Good for: Pistol, Self-defense, Hunting
A typical factory load is a 180 gr JHP bullet at about 1,250 ft/s, with roughly 624 ft-lbs of energy at the muzzle.
Typical load: 180 gr JHP · 5" barrel; Muzzle speed: 1,250 ft/s; Muzzle energy: 624 ft-lbs; Typical BC (G1): ≈ 0.16 typical, varies by brand; Twist rate: 1:16; Practical range: 50 yd hog/deer; Point-blank range: 116 yd 6" vital zone; Recommended platform: Full-size pistol Stout with full-power loads

## .17 Ackley Hornet
URL: https://ammochart.net/cartridges/17-ackley-hornet
P.O. Ackley's improved .22 Hornet necked to .17. Very low noise and recoil for prairie dogs, ground squirrels and foxes on small farms.
Good for: Varmint, Ackley Improved
A typical factory load is a 20 gr V-Max bullet at about 3,650 ft/s, with roughly 592 ft-lbs of energy at the muzzle.
Typical load: 20 gr V-Max; Muzzle speed: 3,650 ft/s; Muzzle energy: 592 ft-lbs; Typical BC (G1): 0.185 maker's published G1; Twist rate: 1:9; Practical range: 250 yd varmint; Point-blank range: 265 yd 4" vital zone; Recommended platform: Any rifle, ultralights included Very light recoil

## .17 HM2
URL: https://ammochart.net/cartridges/17-hm2
.22 LR-length case necked to .17 (Mach 2). Flatter than the .22 LR for squirrels and pests.
Good for: Small game, Pests
A typical factory load is a 17 gr V-Max bullet at about 2,100 ft/s, with roughly 166 ft-lbs of energy at the muzzle.
Typical load: 17 gr V-Max; Muzzle speed: 2,100 ft/s; Muzzle energy: 166 ft-lbs; Typical BC (G1): 0.125 maker's published G1; Twist rate: 1:9; Practical range: 100 yd; Point-blank range: 123 yd 2" vital zone

## .17 HMR
URL: https://ammochart.net/cartridges/17-hmr
.22 WMR necked to .17. Very flat and accurate for prairie dogs, squirrels and pests.
Good for: Small game, Pests, Varmint
A typical factory load is a 17 gr V-Max bullet at about 2,550 ft/s, with roughly 245 ft-lbs of energy at the muzzle.

## .17 WSM
URL: https://ammochart.net/cartridges/17-wsm
The fastest rimfire, built on a nail-gun case. Prairie dogs and coyotes past 200 yd.
Good for: Varmint, Pests
A typical factory load is a 20 gr V-Max bullet at about 3,000 ft/s, with roughly 400 ft-lbs of energy at the muzzle.
Typical load: 20 gr V-Max; Muzzle speed: 3,000 ft/s; Muzzle energy: 400 ft-lbs; Typical BC (G1): 0.185 maker's published G1; Twist rate: 1:9; Practical range: 200 yd; Point-blank range: 181 yd 2" vital zone

## .20 Practical
URL: https://ammochart.net/cartridges/20-practical
.223 brass necked down to .20 cal. Flat, fast and easy on barrels; a favorite prairie dog and coyote round. Forming brass is a single neck-sizing pass.
Good for: Varmint
A typical factory load is a 39 gr Sierra BlitzKing bullet at about 3,500 ft/s, with roughly 1,061 ft-lbs of energy at the muzzle.
Typical load: 39 gr Sierra BlitzKing; Muzzle speed: 3,500 ft/s; Muzzle energy: 1,061 ft-lbs; Typical BC (G1): 0.287 maker's published G1; Twist rate: 1:9 1:8 for 40+ gr; Practical range: 350–400 yd varmint; Point-blank range: 277 yd 4" vital zone; Recommended platform: Any rifle, ultralights included Very light recoil

## .22-250 Ackley Improved
URL: https://ammochart.net/cartridges/22-250-ackley-improved
Blown-out .22-250 with a sharp 40° shoulder for about 100 fps more and longer brass life. Fires factory .22-250 ammo in a pinch.
Good for: Varmint, Ackley Improved
A typical factory load is a 55 gr V-Max bullet at about 3,800 ft/s, with roughly 1,763 ft-lbs of energy at the muzzle.

## 22 ARC
URL: https://ammochart.net/cartridges/22-arc
Hornady's modern answer to the .223: 6mm ARC case necked to .22 for heavy, high-BC bullets. Coyotes and varmints far out, deer where .22s are legal, from an AR-15 or small bolt gun.
Good for: Varmint, Deer/hog
A typical factory load is an 88 gr ELD Match bullet at about 2,820 ft/s, with roughly 1,554 ft-lbs of energy at the muzzle.
Typical load: 88 gr ELD Match; Muzzle speed: 2,820 ft/s; Muzzle energy: 1,554 ft-lbs; Typical BC (G1): 0.545 maker's published G1; Twist rate: 1:7; Practical range: 400+ yd varmint · 250 yd deer; Point-blank range: 243 yd 4" vital zone; Recommended platform: AR-15 or any light rifle Very light recoil

## .22 BR

## .22 LR Subsonic
URL: https://ammochart.net/cartridges/22-lr-subsonic
Stays below the speed of sound, so it's very quiet, especially suppressed. Squirrels, rabbits and pests close in without spooking everything nearby.
Good for: Small game
A typical factory load is a 40 gr hollow point bullet at about 1,050 ft/s, with roughly 98 ft-lbs of energy at the muzzle.

## Comparisons

- [10mm Auto vs .44 Magnum](https://ammochart.net/compare/10mm-auto-vs-44-magnum): With typical loads, the .44 Magnum is about 100 ft/s faster at the muzzle (1,250 vs 1,350 ft/s). The .44 Magnum carries about 56% more energy at the muzzle (971 vs 624 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil.
- [10mm Auto vs .45 ACP](https://ammochart.net/compare/10mm-auto-vs-45-acp): With typical loads, the 10mm Auto is about 400 ft/s faster at the muzzle (1,250 vs 850 ft/s). The 10mm Auto carries about 69% more energy at the muzzle (624 vs 369 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. On the same size target, the 10mm Auto has the longer point-blank range (116 yd), so you can hold dead-on a bit farther without adjusting.
- [.17 HMR vs .22 Long Rifle](https://ammochart.net/compare/17-hmr-vs-22-long-rifle): With typical loads, the .17 HMR is about 1,320 ft/s faster at the muzzle (2,550 vs 1,235 ft/s). The .17 HMR carries about 81% more energy at the muzzle (245 vs 135 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. On the same size target, the .17 HMR has the longer point-blank range (145 yd), so you can hold dead-on a bit farther without adjusting.
- [.17 HMR vs .22 WMR](https://ammochart.net/compare/17-hmr-vs-22-wmr): With typical loads, the .17 HMR is about 640 ft/s faster at the muzzle (2,550 vs 1,910 ft/s). The .22 WMR carries about 32% more energy at the muzzle (324 vs 245 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. On the same size target, the .17 HMR has the longer point-blank range (145 yd), so you can hold dead-on a bit farther without adjusting.
- [.22-250 Remington vs .243 Winchester](https://ammochart.net/compare/22-250-remington-vs-243-winchester): With typical loads, the .22-250 Remington is about 720 ft/s faster at the muzzle (3,680 vs 2,960 ft/s). The .243 Winchester carries about 18% more energy at the muzzle (1,945 vs 1,654 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. The .243 Winchester's typical bullet has the higher BC (0.36), so it holds speed better and drifts less in the wind at long range.
- [.22 Long Rifle vs .22 WMR](https://ammochart.net/compare/22-long-rifle-vs-22-wmr): With typical loads, the .22 WMR is about 680 ft/s faster at the muzzle (1,235 vs 1,910 ft/s). The .22 WMR carries about 140% more energy at the muzzle (324 vs 135 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. On the same size target, the .22 WMR has the longer point-blank range (110 yd), so you can hold dead-on a bit farther without adjusting.
- [.223 Remington vs .22-250 Remington](https://ammochart.net/compare/223-remington-vs-22-250-remington): With typical loads, the .22-250 Remington is about 440 ft/s faster at the muzzle (3,240 vs 3,680 ft/s). The .22-250 Remington carries about 29% more energy at the muzzle (1,654 vs 1,282 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. On the same size target, the .22-250 Remington has the longer point-blank range (284 yd), so you can hold dead-on a bit farther without adjusting.
- [.223 Remington vs 5.56x45 NATO](https://ammochart.net/compare/223-remington-vs-5-56x45-nato): With typical loads, the .223 Remington is about 220 ft/s faster at the muzzle (3,240 vs 3,020 ft/s). Muzzle energy is nearly the same (1,282 vs 1,255 ft-lbs). The 5.56x45 NATO's typical bullet has the higher BC (0.30), so it holds speed better and drifts less in the wind at long range. On the same size target, the 5.56x45 NATO has the longer point-blank range (275 yd), so you can hold dead-on a bit farther without adjusting.
- [.243 Winchester vs .308 Winchester](https://ammochart.net/compare/243-winchester-vs-308-winchester): With typical loads, the .243 Winchester is about 140 ft/s faster at the muzzle (2,960 vs 2,820 ft/s). The .308 Winchester carries about 36% more energy at the muzzle (2,648 vs 1,945 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. The .243 Winchester's typical bullet has the higher BC (0.36), so it holds speed better and drifts less in the wind at long range. On the same size target, the .243 Winchester has the longer point-blank range (283 yd), so you can hold dead-on a bit farther without adjusting.
- [.243 Winchester vs 6.5 Creedmoor](https://ammochart.net/compare/243-winchester-vs-6-5-creedmoor): With typical loads, the .243 Winchester is about 260 ft/s faster at the muzzle (2,960 vs 2,700 ft/s). The 6.5 Creedmoor carries about 19% more energy at the muzzle (2,315 vs 1,945 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. The 6.5 Creedmoor's typical bullet has the higher BC (0.623), so it holds speed better and drifts less in the wind at long range.
- [.25-06 Remington vs .270 Winchester](https://ammochart.net/compare/25-06-remington-vs-270-winchester): With typical loads, the .270 Winchester is about 70 ft/s faster at the muzzle (2,990 vs 3,060 ft/s). The .270 Winchester carries about 16% more energy at the muzzle (2,703 vs 2,322 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil.
- [.270 Winchester vs .30-06 Springfield](https://ammochart.net/compare/270-winchester-vs-30-06-springfield): With typical loads, the .270 Winchester is about 260 ft/s faster at the muzzle (3,060 vs 2,800 ft/s). The .30-06 Springfield carries about 6% more energy at the muzzle (2,872 vs 2,703 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. On the same size target, the .270 Winchester has the longer point-blank range (293 yd), so you can hold dead-on a bit farther without adjusting.
- [.270 Winchester vs 6.5 Creedmoor](https://ammochart.net/compare/270-winchester-vs-6-5-creedmoor): With typical loads, the .270 Winchester is about 360 ft/s faster at the muzzle (3,060 vs 2,700 ft/s). The .270 Winchester carries about 17% more energy at the muzzle (2,703 vs 2,315 ft-lbs), which usually also means more recoil. The 6.5 Creedmoor's typical bullet has the higher BC (0.623), so it holds speed better and drifts less in the wind at long range.
